items.title: NS polls: Anwar shocked by attacks against Anthony Loke during campaigning
items.summary: JELEBU: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he was shocked by the relentless attacks against DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke during the Negri Sembilan election campaign. He described Loke as as an honest and hardworking leader. Every day they attack Loke.

items.title: Federal Court rejects Rosmah’s bid to review judge recusal ruling in solar hybrid graft case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 29 — The Federal Court today dismissed Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s application to review the apex court’s earlier decision dismissing her appeal to recuse Justice Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan, the judge who had presided over her RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project corruption case and convicted her in 2022. Therefore, the application for review is dismissed,” said Justice Azizah, who sat with Federal Court Judges Datuk Lee Swee Seng and Datuk Ravinthran N. Paramaguru. Rosmah’s recusal application was dismissed by the High Court on September 1, 2022, and her appeal was also rejected by the Court of Appeal on September 17 last year.

items.title: Ringgit edges higher against greenback as investors await FOMC outcome
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed marginally higher against the US dollar on Wednesday as investors remained on the sidelines ahead of the outcome of the United States Federal Open Market Committee's (FOMC) meeting. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the ringgit remained largely range-bound against the US dollar, and other Asian currencies showed similar trends, as traders and investors awaited the FOMC's decision later tonight. "West Texas Intermediate and Brent crude oil prices rose by 3.67 per cent and 3.79 per cent to US$82.17 per barrel and US$87.28 per barrel, respectively," he said.

items.title: Police developing system to track repeat traffic offenders
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Federal Police Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) is developing a data system to track repeat traffic offences, including drink-driving cases detected under Op Mabuk. Its director, Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali, said the system would help the department keep track of traffic offenders' records, including whether the offence was their first, second or third violation. "TEID is developing a data system for repeat offence records.

items.title: ‘If there is evidence, they will be charged’: Anwar pledges action after Tabung Haji RCI report release
items.summary: JELEBU, July 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today stressed that any individual found responsible for losses suffered by Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), based on the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report released today, will be brought to justice. He said any elements of misappropriation, fraud and abuse of power identified in the report would be thoroughly investigated by the relevant authorities, including the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and Bank Negara Malaysia. “Those responsible for the losses, fraud and abuse of power will be investigated by the police, the MACC and Bank Negara... everyone will be investigated.

items.title: Regime change? Inside Reza Pahlavi's faltering bid to lead Iran
items.summary: AS the US and Israel went to war on Iran this year, a transformative moment seemed to have arrived for Reza Pahlavi, son of the autocratic shah who was overthrown in 1979. In Texas this March, Pahlavi received one of the most enthusiastic receptions at the Conservative Political Action Conference. Although Batebi supports Pahlavi, he complied.

items.title: From messaging to intelligent engagement: Lessons from a decade in Malaysia
items.summary: THE last decade of customer engagement in Malaysia has proven that digital reach is merely a foundation, not a finish line. Businesses wanted to send alerts, open service channels, launch apps and make themselves easier to contact. It helped bring more customers into digital journeys and made everyday services more accessible.

items.title: Demolition of Sungai Pari Flats rests with appointed developer, says LPHP CEO
items.summary: IPOH, July 29 — The decision on when the long-abandoned Sungai Pari Flats in Buntong will be demolished, and who will carry out the work, rests entirely with the appointed developer, Perak Housing and Property Board (LPHP) chief executive officer Zaiteena Wan Nasir said. Two teenage girls were recently found dead at the flats. The developer is prioritising safety at the site,” she said.

items.title: Reforms start delivering results, says Bank Negara governor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's structural reforms are beginning to pay off, strengthening the economy's fundamentals, attracting higher-quality investments and lifting investor confidence, Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said. "Malaysia recorded its highest-ever investment approvals of around RM431 billion last year, compared with RM384 billion in 2024. Rasheed said investor confidence had also improved, supported by the National Investment Aspirations and Malaysia's efforts to attract investments into strategic, higher-value sectors.

items.title: Fahmi: Pakatan plans 24-hour TikTok livestream to reach young Negeri Sembilan voters
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will intensify its campaign efforts, including holding a continuous TikTok livestream for more than 24 hours to engage young voters ahead of polling day for the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election this Saturday. PH Communications Director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said all PH candidates will continue working to secure victory for the coalition, including winning all 16 seats contested by PKR to strengthen PH’s overall performance in the election. He said this after visiting the Negeri Sembilan bureau of the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama), accompanied by Communications Ministry secretary-general Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah and Bernama Editor-in-Chief Arul Rajoo Durar Raj.

items.title: Selangor plans support for 400 workers affected by Panasonic factory closure
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 29 — The Selangor state government is expected to receive detailed information tomorrow regarding the fate of approximately 400 workers affected by the closure of the television production plant by Panasonic AVC Networks Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Sdn Bhd (PAVCKM) here. Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said that the measure would enable appropriate forms of intervention to be implemented through the cooperation of the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) and the Selangor Labour Department (JTK). Previously, Panasonic Malaysia Sdn.

items.title: Ipoh Sungai Pari Flats block to be demolished after deaths
items.summary: IPOH: The abandoned 15-storey Sungai Pari Flats block, where two schoolgirls were found dead last week after allegedly falling from the building, will be demolished as part of a redevelopment project. Perak Housing and Property Board (LPHP) chief executive officer Zaiteena Wan Nasir said LPHP had appointed a developer to redevelop the site. The developer must also install safety hoarding around the site before any demolition works can commence," she said.

items.title: Bukit Aman busts three drug-laced vape syndicates after students fall ill in Sentul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Police have busted three syndicates involved in the distribution of vape liquids containing synthetic drugs in separate operations across the Klang Valley last Thursday and Saturday. He said that under Op Kesing, Op Madarini and Op Eristalis, police arrested eight men, including two foreign nationals, and six foreign women, aged between 20 and 55, who are believed to be involved in the three syndicates. Police also seized various types of drugs estimated to be worth RM45.6 million.

items.title: Econpile wins RM39mil subcontract for bored piling, substructure works
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Econpile Holdings Bhd has been awarded a subcontract worth RM39.52 million from WCT Construction Sdn Bhd to undertake the earthworks, bored piling and substructure works here at Jalan Awan Besar in Mukim Petaling. Its wholly owned subsidiary, Econpile (M) Sdn Bhd, received the letter of award for the proposed commercial development consisting of four blocks of five-storey commercial shop units, comprising 68 units, two levels of sub-basement car park, and one commercial unit, one main switch station and one refuse chamber. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar: No hiding for those responsible over TH losses
items.summary: JELEBU: Those responsible for losses and abuse of power involving Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) must face investigations and prosecution if there is sufficient evidence. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the cabinet's decision to declassify and release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on TH also included directing enforcement agencies to act on any criminal wrongdoing uncovered. Anwar said TH chairman Tan Sri Rashid Hussain had briefed the cabinet earlier in the day on the RCI's findings, which showed the pilgrimage fund had suffered losses amounting to RM10 billion.

items.title: Experts back proposal for dedicated Maritime Court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Establishing a dedicated Maritime Court would significantly improve legal certainty, enhance Malaysia's standing as a regional maritime legal hub, and strengthen investor confidence in the shipping sector, experts said. Universiti Sains Islam Malaysia Faculty of Syariah and Law International Law Unit head researcher Assoc Prof Dr Mohd Hazmi Mohd Rusli said that while the High Court currently exercises admiralty jurisdiction competently, the highly technical nature of maritime disputes warrants a specialised judicial tribunal. "A dedicated Maritime Court would improve consistency, efficiency, and legal certainty.

items.title: Appeal Court upholds stay on compensation for families of missing pastor Raymond Koh and activist Amri Che Mat
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 29 — The Court of Appeal today upheld the High Court’s decision to stay the execution of a RM37 million damages award to the family of missing pastor Raymond Koh, as well as a RM3 million award to the family of missing activist Amri Che Mat, pending the disposal of the government’s appeals. A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Alwi Abdul Wahab, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman, and Datuk Amarjeet Singh unanimously dismissed the appeals filed by Koh’s wife, Susanna Liew Sow Yoke, and Amri’s wife, Norhayati Ariffin, challenging the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s stay order. In delivering the judgment, Justice Alwi stated that the High Court judge had correctly applied the established principles governing the grant of a stay.

items.title: Zulkifli: RCI report provides opportunity to strengthen Tabung Haji governance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji presents an opportunity to strengthen the pilgrims fund's governance and should be viewed as a catalyst for further reforms rather than a setback for the institution. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the declassification of the report reflected the government's continued commitment to transparency, accountability and good governance. "The findings and recommendations of the RCI should be viewed positively as a valuable opportunity to further strengthen institutions such as Tabung Haji.

items.title: West Bank violence, annexation 'only getting worse': UN
items.summary: GENEVA: Two years after the International Court of Justice said Israel's occupation of the West Bank was unlawful, settler violence and territorial annexation is "only getting worse", the UN said Wednesday. The West Bank has seen near-daily attacks by Israeli settlers and regular raids on Palestinian villages. Overnight Sunday, Palestinian officials said Israeli settlers set fire to two mosques.

items.title: RXZ motorcycle gathering members warned not to flout the law
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: RXZ Members motorcycle gathering participants who commit dangerous riding, reckless acts or traffic offences during may find the police at their doorsteps. Federal Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department (TEID) director Datuk Seri Muhammed Hasbullah Ali said police had prepared recording teams to monitor the convoy, with footage of offences to be reviewed before further action is taken. Hasbullah said the recordings would serve as evidence for police action against participants found breaching traffic laws.

items.title: [UPDATED] Nicky Liow gets DNAA in RM36mil money laundering case after tax settlement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Businessman Nicky Liow has been granted a discharge not amounting to acquittal (DNAA) on 26 money laundering charges involving more than RM36 million after the prosecution withdrew the case. His lawyer, Datuk Rajpal Singh, confirmed that the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) decided not to proceed with the prosecution after Liow, whose full name is Liow Soon Hee, settled RM400,000 in outstanding taxes with the Inland Revenue Board (IRB). However, Liow voluntarily surrendered to the police on April 11, 2022.

items.title: Special Dewan Rakyat sitting needed for MPs to scrutinise Tabung Haji RCI report, says Fahmi
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — The government hopes to hold a special Dewan Rakyat sitting soon to debate the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), as it is an important issue that requires scrutiny by Members of Parliament. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had asked Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said to liaise with Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul to determine the date for the special sitting. Elaborating, Fahmi said today’s Cabinet meeting was briefed by TH chairman and RCI member Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussain on the findings of the inquiry.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar: Myanmar agrees to take back 5,000 Rohingya from Malaysia
items.summary: JELEBU: Myanmar has agreed to accept an initial group of 5,000 Rohingya from Malaysia following negotiations between the two governments, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the move was part of broader efforts to address the long-running Rohingya issue while maintaining public order in Malaysia. Anwar said Myanmar was also taking back 300,000 Rohingya from Bangladesh, describing the development as the result of diplomatic negotiations.

items.title: Tabung Haji welcomes release of RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has welcomed the government's decision to release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into its management. "TH has already taken note of the RCI recommendations on what happened in the past prior to 2018. TH has since moved on," it said in a statement.

items.title: Selangor JPJ seizes 34 vehicles in crackdown on unlicensed foreign drivers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The Selangor Road Transport Department (JPJ) seized 34 vehicles in a joint operation with the Selayang Municipal Council (MPS) targeting foreign drivers this morning. Selangor JPJ director Datuk Ahmad Kamarunzaman Menhat said 126 vehicles were checked during the operation, which began at 6.30am. The operation in Selayang involved 55 JPJ officers and personnel, supported by 25 MPS officers.

items.title: Making local a natural choice
items.summary: LETTERS: The government's effort to rebrand the four-decade-old 'Buy Malaysian Goods' campaign into 'Jom Beli Produk Malaysia' (Jom Malaysia) is a welcome move. As an ongoing national effort, it also raises an important question - what will persuade consumers to continue choosing local in the long run? It should encourage businesses to keep improving their products while giving consumers more reasons to choose Malaysian products with confidence.

items.title: Fahmi says PAS is using fear over Malay representation in Negeri Sembilan campaign
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 — The claim that Pakatan Harapan (PH)’s victory in the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election will lead to the redelineation of the State Legislative Assembly constituencies, thus reducing Malay and Muslim power, is an unhealthy campaign that is trying to scare the people. He said this when commenting on claims by PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan that PH’s victory in Negeri Sembilan has the potential to change the state’s political landscape through an increase in the number of state assembly seats. Takiyuddin reportedly said that the state assembly constituencies that have a large number of voters and is currently represented by PH is likely to be split into several new constituencies in the future.

items.title: Zimbabwe explores media cooperation with Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zimbabwe is looking to forge media cooperation with Malaysia through a proposed memorandum of understanding (MoU), with talks at an advanced stage. Zimbabwe's Permanent Secretary for Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services, Nick Mangwana, said most of the proposed MoU's provisions had already been agreed upon, paving the way for collaboration in digital transformation, broadcasting, news operations and professional exchanges during an official visit to Media Prima Berhad's News and Current Affairs division. Accompanied by representatives from Zimbabwe's Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Ministry, Mangwana said the visit to Media Prima was part of the delegation's official programme in Malaysia to strengthen bilateral ties and explore collaboration between the two countries' media sectors.

items.title: NS polls: Fahmi warns against fake news on WhatsApp
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The public has been urged to be wary of fake news related to the Negri Sembilan election, particularly content circulated via WhatsApp. PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said his team had observed a surge in content being shared without links, consisting only of images and videos. Fahmi said the public should verify whether official and mainstream media had reported the information being circulated.

items.title: CAAM urges West Asia-bound passengers to check flights as airlines suspend, reroute services
items.summary: CAAM, in a statement today, said airlines may reroute flights, revise schedules or cancel certain services, and these operational adjustments may result in longer flight times, delays or disruptions to connecting flights. It said several airlines have announced temporary suspensions, cancellations or adjustments to services involving destinations in West Asia. CAAM said Malaysia Airlines’ Kuala Lumpur-Doha flight is operating daily while other Doha services are suspended until Oct 24.

items.title: Bukit Aman steps up roadblocks, but Malaysia’s drunk driving arrests barely increase
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Traffic police made over 900 arrests for drunk or intoxicated driving between January and June this year, just marginally higher than the same period last year, despite a nearly threefold increase in enforcement operations. Individuals aged 41 and above recorded the highest number of arrests, at 364 people or 38.4 per cent of total arrests by age group. Arrests involving 16 to 20 years old totalled seven people, or 0.7 per cent.

items.title: [UPDATED] Suspended cop among 5 held as police seize RM21.3m in meth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A suspended police officer is believed to have masterminded a drug trafficking syndicate dealing in methamphetamine for both the local and international markets. Police seized 425.3kg of methamphetamine that were packed into 410 plastic packets. He said police had identified other members of the syndicate.

items.title: Anwar calls for massive investment, regional cooperation to drive Asean energy transition
items.summary: He said achieving the energy transition at scale would require unprecedented collaboration among the public sector, private investors and project developers to mobilise the financing needed. “It is central to strengthening Malaysia and the region’s energy security. Anwar also said that energy transition does not proceed on a straight line, nor can integration proceed in isolation.

items.title: Negri polls: Fahmi praises Media Prima election coverage operations
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil praised Media Prima Bhd's (MPB) performance, highlighting the company's professionalism in managing operations during the Negri Sembilan state election. Fahmi said MPB had made effective use of its existing equipment while adopting new technology to help manage production costs throughout its election coverage. "What Media Prima has demonstrated is quite impressive because, if we watch its television broadcasts or social media coverage, it is clearly professional.

items.title: [UPDATED] Rosmah loses final bid to review recusal of judge in solar hybrid corruption case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor has failed in her bid to review the Federal Court's decision refusing to disqualify the judge who convicted her in the RM1.25 billion solar hybrid project corruption case. On March 3, a separate Federal Court panel dismissed her final bid to recuse then High Court judge Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan, who has since been elevated to the Court of Appeal. Azizah, when reading the unanimous decision, said the court found no failure by the earlier Federal Court to properly discharge its judicial functions, contrary to Rosmah's contention.

items.title: Kidnap victim directly involved in local drug trafficking syndicate, say police
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The 44-year-old man who was kidnapped in a case involving a RM7 million ransom demand is believed to have been directly involved in a local drug trafficking syndicate. Federal police Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigations were ongoing to identify other members of the network. "The victim is believed to have been directly involved in a local drug trafficking syndicate," he told reporters.

items.title: Prasarana targets 1.7m daily riders by 2027, says 377,000 vehicles kept off roads in 2025
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Prasarana Malaysia Berhad (Prasarana) is aiming to increase its average daily ridership to 1.7 million passengers by 2027 by improving the reliability and availability of its rail and bus services, while encouraging more people to shift away from private vehicles. Prasarana Group Chairman Tan Sri Mohd Nasir Ahmad said the target is based on the company’s encouraging performance, having recorded an average of 1.3 million passenger trips per day last year. He said Prasarana would continue prioritising service reliability and availability to ensure its trains and buses remain the preferred mode of transport for commuters.

items.title: Petronas, Hokuriku renew long-term LNG pact
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas LNG Ltd has signed a heads of agreement with Hokuriku Electric Power Company to renew their long-term liquified natural gas (LNG) supply agreement. Petronas LNG is expected to continue supplying up to 0.54 million tonnes per annum of LNG to Hokuriku Electric for 10 years from 2028. The agreement was signed on July 14 by Petronas LNG chief executive officer (CEO) Rosdi Ab Rahman and Hokuriku Electric president Koji Matsuda.

items.title: Russia seeks arrest of Telegram chief Durov
items.summary: MOSCOW: Russia announced on Wednesday that it was seeking the arrest of Telegram founder Pavel Durov over accusations of "complicity in terrorism", alleging he had let the platform be used for recruitment by Ukraine's security services. The FSB security service said it had launched international search proceedings for Durov, who is also Telegram's CEO. "An international wanted notice has been issued... for the head of the Telegram administration, P. Durov," it said in a statement.

items.title: Prosecution reclassifies case against drink-driver after delivery rider dies
items.summary: The accused, Low Kean Peng, 35, will face a fresh charge after the victim, Zulfiqar Zamir Amirul Nizam, 27, died while receiving treatment in hospital. In a statement today, the Klang Selatan district police headquarters said the prosecution had ordered the case to be reclassified and that Low would be charged again at the Klang Court Complex tomorrow. Low's lawyer, Ethan W.H.

items.title: Tabung Haji welcomes RCI report release, but says it has ‘already moved on’
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has embraced the government’s decision to release the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report to the public, asserting that it has already addressed the commission’s findings on events prior to 2018 and has “since moved on.” In a statement issued today, the pilgrims’ fund board revealed that it has already implemented 75 per cent of the RCI’s recommendations. Crucially, the government has also ordered enforcement agencies to launch immediate investigations into the report’s findings to ensure any lawbreakers are brought to justice. The release of the report ends a period of strategic secrecy.

items.title: KTMB puts on additional Komuter and ETS services ahead of Negri polls
items.summary: For ETS services, KTMB will provide 30 additional trips involving the KL Sentral–JB Sentral–KL Sentral routes (12 trips), JB Sentral–Seremban–JB Sentral (12 trips) and KL Sentral–Padang Besar–KL Sentral (six trips) with a total of 9,480 seats. For the JB Sentral–Seremban–JB Sentral route, train EP9636 is scheduled to depart from JB Sentral on 2.10pm and arrives in Seremban at 5.15pm, while EP9637 departs from Seremban at 5.45pm and arrives at JB Sentral at 8.50pm. For the JB Sentral–KL Sentral–JB Sentral route, the departure time from JB Sentral is at 7am via train EX9572 (arrives 11.10am) and 5.30pm for EX9578 (arrives 9.40pm).

items.title: Prosecutors say Charlie Kirk was attacked for his politics, cite anti-LGBT views
items.summary: UTAH: Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing Charlie Kirk, targeted the right-wing activist for his political views, prosecutors said on Tuesday, citing Kirk's opposition to gay marriage and transgender rights. "The circumstantial evidence that Defendant targeted Mr. Kirk because of Defendant's belief or perception of Mr. Kirk's political beliefs is overwhelming," prosecutors said in their written argument on why there is sufficient evidence to try Robinson for Kirk's murder. Robinson's lawyer Richard Novak said in court on July 9 that Engelhardt's letter gave no evidence Robinson disagreed with Kirk's political or religious views and shed no light on Robinson's state of mind.

items.title: 206 investors obtain default judgment against Allan Goh and companies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Businessman Datuk Allan Goh has been ordered by the High Court to repay RM67.56 million to 206 investors after the court found that he controlled an illegal deposit-taking and Ponzi scheme operated through the I-Serve "ecosystem". The court ruled that the defendants were jointly and severally liable to refund the investors' deposits amounting to RM67,556,087, together with interest, damages to be assessed, and RM80,000 in costs. The court declared that Goh was the controlling mind behind the I-Serve ecosystem, which operated as a single economic unit and constituted an illegal deposit-taking scheme and/or a Ponzi or pyramid scheme.

items.title: Cabinet agrees to extend Act 672 to all 12 Selangor local authorities
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, July 29 — The Cabinet has agreed to extend the application of the Solid Waste and Public Cleansing Management Act 2007 (Act 672) to Selangor on a phased basis, covering all 12 local authorities in the state, said Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. Nga added that, in line with the Cabinet decision and the National Public Cleansing Policy, the Madani government is committed to implementing public cleansing reforms under the 13th Malaysia Plan. Nga also said that waste collection and cleansing operations will shift to nighttime schedules.

items.title: 18 WTE projects approved by 2040, to generate 600MW of renewable energy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 18 waste-to-energy (WTE) projects have been approved for development by 2040, as the government ramps up long-term efforts to modernise solid waste management and boost renewable energy generation. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming said the projects, planned by the National Solid Waste Management Department, are expected to generate up to 600 megawatts of renewable energy. He said WTE technology is widely used in developed countries as an efficient and sustainable method of managing solid waste.

items.title: Warisan files notice of appeal after Shafie Apdal’s contempt conviction
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 29 — Parti Warisan president Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal is challenging his conviction and five-week jail sentence for contempt of court over remarks made regarding the inquest into the death of 13-year-old Zara Qairina Mahathir. The party confirmed today that its legal team will immediately file a notice of appeal to the High Court. While Sessions Court Judge Amir Shah Amir Hassan found the former Sabah chief minister guilty of contempt, the court stayed the execution of the prison sentence, allowing Shafie to remain free pending the appeal.

items.title: PDRM announces transfer of 26 senior officers, including new Sabah, Selangor and Sarawak CID chiefs
items.summary: He said Head of the E6 Special Branch, Bukit Aman, DCP Datuk Mohd Taufik Toh Abdullah has been appointed Deputy Director I of the Special Branch, also with the acting rank of CP. Mohamad Noor said the transfers also involve Assistant Director E4A of the Special Branch, Bukit Aman, SAC Roslan Alias, who has been appointed Head of the E6 Special Branch, Bukit Aman, with the acting rank of DCP. He said SAC Lim San Aik, currently the Sarawak CID chief, has been appointed Sabah Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department chief, while Kuala Lumpur Special Branch deputy chief (Intelligence/Operations) ACP Kamaruzaman Md Alib has been appointed Assistant Director E1A of the Special Branch, Bukit Aman, with the acting rank of SAC.

items.title: Fahmi: Cabinet orders full and immediate probes in Tabung Haji RCI case
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil announced today that the Cabinet has agreed to fast-track such investigations based on the RCI report to ensure that those involved are brought to justice. The announcement follows a confirmation from Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim earlier today that the government is moving toward full disclosure. In a move toward transparency, Fahmi said the Cabinet has also agreed to declassify the RCI report and unveil it to the public.

items.title: Nicky Liow denies PKR membership claims, says AMK shirt was bought at charity sale
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Businessman Datuk Seri Nicky Liow Soon Hee today denied claims that he is a member of PKR, saying speculation sparked by a viral photograph of him standing beside Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was unfounded. Purchasing and wearing a uniform sold at a public fundraising event should not be directly interpreted as joining a political party, nor should it be used as a basis to infer a person’s political identity or political stance. “Wearing a shirt distributed at a public event should not be interpreted as joining a political party, nor should it be used to infer anyone’s political identity,” said Liow.

items.title: Trial: Bersatu finance officer confirms party received donations; finances reported to leadership including Muhyiddin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — Donations that had been given to Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia have to be declared to the party's supreme council, which is the party's highest executive body that also includes party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, the High Court heard today. Based on Bersatu's party constitution's Article 23.2.1, Zulhelmi said each financial contribution to the party has to be declared to the party's supreme council. Zulhelmi : Yes.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI report set for public release today, Anwar confirms
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, July 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has confirmed that the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) is set to be released to the public today. “Yes, yes,” Anwar said when asked if the document would be published today. Last week, Anwar explained that the previous administration withheld the findings to avoid undermining public confidence in the pilgrims’ fund board.

items.title: KL police transfer 113 refugees to new locations in three states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — All 113 refugees temporarily housed at the Kuala Lumpur Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) were transferred in stages yesterday following a document re-identification process, Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said. He said the refugees were bound for destinations in Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, and Penang, as determined by non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) based on the locations of their relatives and acquaintances. Fadil said 66 refugees were transferred to destinations in Kuala Lumpur, while 29 were transferred to Selangor and 18 to Penang.

items.title: Malaysia tightens hiking rules to cut costly mountain rescue operations
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) is tightening controls on hiking activities nationwide, including restricting “day hikes” or “compressed hikes” in high-risk mountainous areas, to reduce accidents and the need for costly search and rescue (SAR) operations. Its Deputy Minister, Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh, said some hikers continue to underestimate the importance of proper preparation, while others are driven by social media trends or venture onto unauthorised trails, increasing the risk of emergencies and hikers getting lost in the forest. Syed Ibrahim said the Forestry Department of Peninsular Malaysia (JPSM) has also made the services of Forestry Mountain Guides (MGP) mandatory at 189 high-risk hiking locations nationwide.

items.title: Malaysia needs at least RM300m a year to secure permanent F1 return, says SIC CEO
items.summary: SEPANG, July 29 — Malaysia would need to spend at least RM300 million annually if it hopes to secure a permanent place on the Formula 1 (F1) world championship calendar, according to Sepang International Circuit (SIC) Chief Executive Officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif. He said the estimate covers Formula 1 hosting rights fees, currently estimated at between US$70 million and US$80 million (RM289 million to RM340 million), as well as local preparation costs required to meet the specifications for staging the prestigious race. He said there are two main requirements if Malaysia is to regain a permanent slot on the Formula 1 calendar: the ability to pay the hosting rights fees and the availability of a slot on the championship calendar.

items.title: Chow Kon Yeow: Penang to respond only after Kedah submits formal lease payment claim
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 29 — Penang will continue to wait for Kedah to formally submit its claim over the state’s lease payments before responding, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. He said this was not the first time Kedah Mentri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor had spoken about pursuing a revision of Penang’s lease payment rates. Asked whether the issue could strain relations between Penang and Kedah if the claim proceeds, Chow said it was premature to comment as Penang had yet to receive any formal demand.

items.title: Prasarana says 1.31 million daily riders helped avoid 225,000 tonnes of carbon emissions in 2025
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, July 29 — Prasarana Malaysia Berhad today announced that it avoided an estimated 225,000 tonnes of carbon emissions in 2025, based on public transport usage averaging 1.31 million passenger trips a day. Amir said the report, themed The City on the Move, is the first sustainability report published in Prasarana’s 28-year history. “Today, sustainability goes beyond environmental sustainability.

items.title: Police investigate Jempol MP after report over allegedly seditious campaign speech
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 29 —Police have opened an investigation paper against Jempol Member of Parliament Datuk Shamsulkahar Mohd Deli over a campaign speech in Seremban Jaya which was alleged to contain seditious elements. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the investigation was launched following a report lodged by a 55-year-old man who was dissatisfied with a social media video post showing the politician’s campaign speech. For the latest updates on the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, visit https://prn.bernama.com/n9.

items.title: Spending controls yield nearly RM5b savings without affecting key services, says Liew Chin Tong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 29 — The government has recorded nearly RM5 billion in savings as of July 14, 2026, from the implementation of expenditure control measures following the RM10 billion adjustment to the operating expenditure allocation for this year, said Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong. Liew said the Ministry of Finance (MOF) on April 29, 2026, issued directives to adjust allocations across all ministries and government agencies before holding engagement sessions to explain the expenditure control criteria needed to be implemented in response to the global supply chain crisis. He noted that the expenditure control measures implemented by the government in the first half of 2026 successfully improved the efficiency of public financial management without compromising the delivery of critical services to the people or the country’s economic stability.

items.title: Three surveyors found safe after getting lost during forest survey in Dungun
items.summary: DUNGUN, July 29 — Three male surveyors who were reported to have lost their way while carrying out land surveying work in a forest area in Kampung Tok Kah here were found safe in a search and rescue (SAR) operation last night. Dungun district police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the victims, Wan Muhamad Haziem Wan Abdullah, 32, Wan Hafizuddin Aiman Wan Zamili, 23, and Muhammad Adam Ruzilan, 22, were found at 11.30 pm. He said the three victims entered the forest area at 10 am yesterday with three other colleagues to carry out land surveying work, before they split into two groups at the location.
